final_output:
## 1. Short answer
The maximum levels listed for dried figs are **6 μg/kg for aflatoxin B1** and **10 μg/kg for the sum of aflatoxins B1, B2, G1 and G2**.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions
Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, Section 1.1, row 1.1.3 (“Dried figs”) gives those limits. The sum-of-aflatoxins maximum is calculated on a **lower-bound** basis: values below the limit of quantification are treated as zero.

The row also says these limits apply to food consisting only of dried figs and to processed products consisting of at least 80% dried figs. For other products, the Regulation’s Article 3(1) and (2) apply.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed
EU Cellar metadata identifies 19 August 2026 as the latest observed consolidation date for Regulation 2023/915. That metadata does **not** verify article-level changes, application dates or current legal status. Before relying on the figures for a shipment decision, check the applicable consolidated text, any amendments and transitional provisions, and confirm the product’s classification as dried figs intended for direct consumption.
